findings.title: Hearing is not yet reception
findings.claim: Across the wider parallels, audible attention can fail to reach understanding or lead into discernment and following. In 17:47 the act of listening is placed beside a hostile description of what its hearers supposedly follow, making reception itself contested rather than absent.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the repeated yastami'una ilayk forms and the following verb in the quoted accusation. In 10:42 and 6:25, listening to the messenger is explicitly set beside blocked understanding; 39:18 pairs listening to speech with following its best, while 46:29 depicts attentive listening that leads to silence and warning. These independent contrasts contact the focus's hearing and following, separating acoustic exposure from uptake.
findings.reader_payoff: The dispute is not simply whether the audience heard the message: the focus makes the direction assigned to listening and following part of the accusation.
findings.containment: The parallels are contrasts, not identical audiences or proof of what the focus listeners intend. Connection targets supply exact Arabic but not target morphology or lexical analysis, so no morphology is inferred and the comparison remains contextual.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication and exact focus carriers support the reading, and supplied target Arabic gives concrete positive and negative reception contrasts. The represented HFT summary is unanchored and not used as sole evidence; target morphology is absent from the connection records.

findings.title: Private counsel turns hearing into a public counter-frame
findings.claim: In 17:47 listening is followed by secret counsel and a public bewitched-man label. Wider parallels connect secret consultation with hostile appraisal of a messenger, and one explicit parallel ties that transition to an aim of expulsion. This makes a collective speech circuit, and a possible mobilizing counter-frame, a live reading of the focus rather than treating private counsel as neutral privacy.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the listening forms, the collective najwa, the designation of the speakers as wrongdoers, and the quoted mas'hur label. 21:3 joins secret whisper by wrongdoers to a human-messenger and magic challenge; 20:62-63 moves from secret dispute to a sorcerer accusation and an expressed wish to expel; 58:8 describes counsel in sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger. 25:8 repeats the bewitched-man label and 54:2 shows a seen sign being dismissed as magic. These independent contacts connect private counsel and the label to contested reception and hostile public framing.
findings.reader_payoff: The sequence can be read as social interpretation: what was heard is discussed, then recoded through a label that may mobilize opposition to the messenger.
findings.containment: The wider episodes do not establish shared actors or coordination, and the expulsion aim in 20:63 belongs to that passage's speakers only. The focus does not prove the accusation false or settle whether its magic language is literal; 43:49 uses a magician address in a plea, and 10:77 disputes a magic charge. The legacy walk's reading of 17:45-46 and 17:48 is attributed to that source. Connection target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication supplies the focus-level counter-frame, while exact connection Arabic independently grounds counsel, magic-label, and expulsion parallels. Legacy support adds a wider speech-circuit inference and the 17:45-48 reading; these are retained with explicit attribution and containment.

findings.title: The accusation recurs after signs
findings.claim: The focus's bewitched-man label recurs at 17:101 after the text mentions nine clear signs. This recurrence supports the retrospective reading of the label as a durable political defense against cumulative evidence, rather than an isolated insult.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the mas'hur label at 17:47:19:1; the independent trigger is 17:101, where Pharaoh's accusation follows the mention of nine clear signs. Their contact makes the accusation legible as a recurring counter-description that can divert attention from evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The same label can be seen as a way to account for a messenger instead of engaging the signs associated with him.
findings.containment: This is a qualified inference from recurrence. It does not establish the same speakers, a causal history, a shared political plan, or that the focus audience saw the same signs; target morphology and lexical analysis at 17:101 are not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The legacy retrospective names 17:101, and the connection supplies its exact Arabic including the nine-sign context and bewitched label. The broader political-defense mechanism remains an inference, not a proven shared intention.

findings.title: Human messengership as an objection
findings.claim: The focus calls the person said to be followed a man, while 17:94 reports an objection to belief because God sent a human as messenger. This permits a bounded wider reading in which the focus's bewitched-man label participates in a recurrent dismissal of a human messenger.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is rajulan at 17:47:18:1. The independent trigger is the exact wording in 17:94 asking whether God sent a bashar as messenger. The category-level contact makes the focus's man-plus-bewitched description readable as a two-part source objection: human identity and alleged impairment.
findings.reader_payoff: The label can be heard as discrediting both the messenger's human status and his claimed condition, rather than as a free-standing diagnosis.
findings.containment: This is an analogy between the focus's man and 17:94's human-messenger objection, not an assertion that the terms are lexically identical, that the speakers are the same, or that every human-messenger reference is hostile. Target morphology and lexical analysis are absent.

epistemic.reason: The focus word and supplied 17:94 Arabic support a limited category-level analogy, but the connection is a nomination and provides no target morphology or lexical analysis.
